propositions: Rebar's bespoke structured-output orchestration must be replaced with Pydantic AI seams while preserving historical behavior around deterministic repair, extraction, refusal/truncation handling, retry and tool/request limits, per-operation budgets, provider fallback, usage accounting, and failure taxonomy

An offline integration probe exercising real Pydantic AI 1.107.2 Agent/output/retry/limits/hooks seams with mocked provider transport confirmed 19/19 scenarios pass and established exact behavioral oracles for native mode, prompted mode, repairable rejection, output retry, request limits, tool limits, fallback predicates, content-filter handling, and cumulative usage

Material behavioral deltas identified across request-budget semantics, retry-message wire shape, successful-retry usage aggregation, output-exhaustion exception translation, and underlying attempt accounting must be explicitly classified as preserve, intentionally change, or require maintainer decision rather than silently inherited

Retry-loop ownership (Pydantic versus Rebar), retry-wire truncation policy, and successful-retry usage accounting remain pending maintainer decisions with exact constraints: preserve three total attempts, early success, deterministic repair/extraction, stop-reason fast-fail, cumulative usage, public failure translation, and final-failure-only artifact timing

Cache-impact validation with live Anthropic and Bedrock calls confirmed same-run retry read 1,536 more cached tokens and wrote 1,532 fewer, and revealed that complete failed responses on retry have correctness risk when tail contains valid material findings omitted from prefix-truncated versions

Three recommendations approved without new maintainer choices: aggregate successful retry usage across all consumer paths, narrowly translate only Rebar-owned output errors found in Pydantic's cause chain, and add truthful logical candidate-request count to diagnostics and durable operation rows without redefining request-limit semantics
